To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a sequential processing method using an extended Kalman filter is a promising approach to estimate the ocean surface wind field from GNSS reflectometry measurements and that the method is able to meet the CYGNS mission measurement requirements.
the EKF approach to sequential processing of DDMs to estimate the wind field over a swath is feasible and that it can produce wind speed retrievals that meet the CYGNUS measurement requirements.

sequential processing of GNSS R DDMs can be used to improve wind retrievals by exploiting the spatial and temporal correlation of the wind field, and that this method is capable of meeting the CYGNSS wind retrieval requirements for hurricane force winds.
In summary, our research is concerned with

developing a method to process GNSS R data in the presence of spatially varying winds and demonstrates that sequential processing can improve wind retrievals over the large swath required by the CYGNSS mission.
the processing of GNSS R delay Doppler maps to retrieve wind fields.
the development of an algorithm that can be used to retrieve wind speeds at a higher resolution than the 25 km CYGNSS resolution requirement.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the sequential processing approach is a viable method to retrieve the ocean surface wind field using the DDMs from the CYGNSS mission.
the sequential approach is a viable alternative to single point retrievals for the CYGNSS mission.
the EKF method is capable of retrieving wind speeds with a 2 m/s accuracy within a swath of 90 km, and 10% accuracy within a swath 20 km.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

sequential processing of DDMs can be used to improve the spatial resolution of GNSS R wind retrievals and that it can be used in a limited data budget to improve the wind retrieval performance for low wind speeds and within a larger swath.
the proposed sequential processing method can improve the wind speed estimation by using the full DDM information.
sequential processing of GNSS-R delay Doppler maps can improve wind retrieval accuracy over a large swath of the ocean surface and can be used to improve wind retrievals at the GNSS-R specular point.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CYGNSS wind speed requirement can be met within the $90\times90$ km swath using a combination of the EKF and a larger portion of each DDM.
the wind field can be retrieved from a much larger portion of the delay Dopple map than the specular point alone.
the wind speed can be estimated over a swath using a series of DMMs, which may be useful for future GNSS-R missions with larger glistening zones.
